An electroluminescence device includes a base material having a recessed portion formed therein. A light-emitting element is provided in association with the recessed portion and includes a reflective layer, a transparent filling layer, a transparent first electrode, an organic light-emitting layer, and a transparent second electrode.

The reflective layer is disposed within or along the recessed portion of the base material and is configured to reflect light generated by the organic light-emitting layer. The transparent filling layer is formed over the reflective layer and fills at least part of the recessed portion, thereby providing a surface on which the transparent first electrode can be arranged. The transparent first electrode is disposed over the transparent filling layer, and the organic light-emitting layer is formed over the transparent first electrode. The transparent second electrode is provided over the organic light-emitting layer. In this structure, light generated in the organic light-emitting layer can be emitted through the transparent electrodes, while the reflective layer improves light extraction by reflecting light in a desired direction.

The device further includes an active element electrically connected to the light-emitting element. The active element controls the light-emitting operation of the light-emitting element, for example by regulating the current supplied to the organic light-emitting layer. In this way, each light-emitting element can be selectively driven according to display signals.

A display region of the electroluminescence device is divided into a plurality of unit regions. Each unit region includes a plurality of light-emitting elements and a plurality of active elements corresponding to those light-emitting elements. The active elements are arranged to individually or collectively control the emission of light from the light-emitting elements within each unit region, thereby enabling image display over the display region.

In at least one of the light-emitting elements, the reflective layer also serves as a contact portion electrically connected to the active element. By allowing the reflective layer to function as both a light-reflecting member and an electrical contact, the device structure can be simplified, the number of separate conductive components can be reduced, and efficient electrical connection between the active element and the light-emitting element can be achieved.
outputs.L4:
An electroluminescence device includes a base material having a plurality of recessed portions formed therein. In each recessed portion, a light-emitting element is provided by arranging a transparent electrode, an organic electroluminescent light-emitting layer, a filling layer, and a reflective layer. The transparent electrode is disposed so that light generated in the organic light-emitting layer can be emitted through the transparent electrode side, while the reflective layer reflects light toward the emission side, thereby improving light extraction efficiency.

The device is divided into a plurality of display unit regions, each of which may correspond to a pixel or sub-pixel region. In each display unit region, a plurality of light-emitting elements can be arranged and individually or collectively controlled. Active elements, such as thin-film transistors, are provided in association with the display unit regions and are used to control the supply of current to the respective light-emitting elements. By controlling the active elements, the emission state, brightness, and timing of each light-emitting element can be adjusted, enabling the device to function as an active-matrix electroluminescence display.

The recessed portions of the base material serve to define and accommodate the structural layers of the light-emitting elements. By forming the transparent electrodes, organic light-emitting layers, filling layers, and reflective layers within these recessed portions, the device can achieve a compact and highly integrated pixel structure. The filling layer may be provided to planarize the recessed portion, protect the organic light-emitting layer, or improve optical and mechanical characteristics of the light-emitting element.

At least one of the reflective layers is also used as a contact portion electrically connected to an active element. In this configuration, the reflective layer performs both an optical function and an electrical function. It reflects light generated by the organic light-emitting layer while also serving as a conductive path between the light-emitting element and the corresponding active element. This dual use reduces the need for separate wiring or contact structures, thereby simplifying the device layout and allowing the display unit regions to be made smaller and more densely arranged.

Because the reflective layer can function as part of the electrical connection to the active element, the overall pixel structure can be formed with fewer components and reduced space requirements. This contributes to improved aperture ratio, enhanced display resolution, and more efficient use of the available substrate area. The structure is particularly suitable for compact electroluminescence displays in which multiple light-emitting elements are integrated within each display unit region and are actively controlled to produce high-quality images.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. When we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are referring to a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence. For example, “The sun is shining” tells us exactly which sun we mean. “The teacher entered the classroom” points to a specific teacher and a specific classroom. Without “the,” many sentences would sound incomplete or less precise.

“The” is also one of the most commonly used words in English. It appears in everyday conversations, books, articles, songs, and speeches. Although it is short, it connects ideas and makes communication smoother.

In many ways, “the” shows that even the smallest words can have a big impact. It reminds us that language depends not only on large and impressive words, but also on simple ones that help us understand each other clearly.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an electroluminescence device according to a disclosure, using formal patent wording, in which a reflective layer is formed on the front surface of a recessed portion and doubles as a contact to an active element.
counterfactuals.output:
An electroluminescence device comprising:

a substrate having a recessed portion formed in a front surface thereof;

an active element provided on the substrate and including a terminal electrode;

an electroluminescence element disposed at least partly in correspondence with the recessed portion and including a first electrode, an electroluminescent layer, and a second electrode; and

a reflective layer formed on a front surface of the recessed portion,

wherein the reflective layer is electrically connected to the terminal electrode of the active element and is configured to function both as a light-reflecting member for reflecting light emitted from the electroluminescence element and as a contact electrode for electrically coupling the active element to the electroluminescence element.

In one embodiment, the reflective layer is formed of a conductive light-reflective material, such as aluminum, silver, an aluminum alloy, or a silver alloy, and is disposed along an inner surface of the recessed portion so as to define a reflective concave surface. The reflective layer may be connected to a drain or source electrode of a thin-film transistor constituting the active element, and may further be connected to the first electrode of the electroluminescence element, whereby current supplied from the active element is applied to the electroluminescence element through the reflective layer.

Accordingly, the reflective layer serves a dual function as an optical reflector and as an electrical contact, thereby reducing the number of separately formed conductive layers and improving light extraction efficiency from the electroluminescence device.
